integration_issues.flow: Kasgeld auto-print to KT-V520 (1 or 2 printers)
integration_issues.issue: Race condition. trackKtpJob(job_id) only runs AFTER the POST /kiosk/kasgeld/{id}/remote-print response returns. The printer's REMOTE_PRINT_DONE can arrive over the kiosk WS before that (we measured the HTTP response only about 60ms ahead of the ack). The ack is then dropped ('if (!job) return' in KtpPrintToast.jsx). Result: the green toast is missing or only names one printer, and after 20s a misleading red 'Geen antwoord van <printer>' appears even though the bon printed. Seen in about 2 of 5 runs with 2 printers and 1 of 2 runs with 1 printer, using a fake printer that acks instantly. A real V520 acks slower, so it is less frequent but still possible. The same pattern affects KtpPrintButton and PrintChoiceMenu.

action_items: MEDIUM: fix the ack race in KtpPrintToast.jsx. In the 'ktp-remote-print-done' listener, buffer unmatched job_ids for about 30s (e.g. a Map early.set(job_id, detail)). In trackKtpJob, first check the buffer: if the ack is already there, dispatch the toast immediately and do not start the 20s 'Geen antwoord' timer. Alternative: let the client generate the job_id, register it before the POST, and send it in the body.
critical_code_review_comments: kiosk_create_cash verifies the employee PIN correctly against kiosk_pin_hash, scoped to company_id and active=True. A wrong PIN falls back silently, which matches the spec. Note: the PIN travels in the query string (it can end up in proxy/access logs). Existing withKioskEmployee pattern, so acceptable, but a header or body field would be safer.
KtpPrintToast merge logic works. Names are deduped, and a merge only happens while the previous toast is still an ok toast. It is order-dependent (A en B vs B en A), which is cosmetic.

success_rate.frontend: Employee name 100%. Merged toast works, but it is flaky because of the ack race (about 40% of runs show a missing or partial toast). Payment toast regression passes.
